title: Structural load-path, review, inspection, and records assumptions can fail before critical state becomes legible
summary: Candidate pattern for structural/civil failures in which the decisive structural state is hidden from, or not acted upon by, design review, peer review, inspection, maintenance, records, or reporting/correction rails.

status_history.note: Created after promoting first structural failure lane records and infrastructure rails.

subjects.name: structural load-path legibility and correction rails

claims.claim: Hyatt, I-35W, FIU, Fern Hollow, and Champlain together support a candidate structural-failure pattern: critical load-path or condition assumptions become dangerous when design review, peer review, inspection, maintenance action, records, or open-investigation status fails to make the decisive structural state legible.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: NIST DFS/NCST, FHWA NBIS, NTSB infrastructure investigations, and CROSS-US are visibility or correction rails for this pattern, but none by itself proves that design errors, distress, corrosion, records, or maintenance recommendations will be detected and corrected.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: MKH-PAT-0020 must remain candidate-level because it currently lacks positive controls where review/inspection/reporting rails intercepted a structural hazard before failure and negative controls where similar rails or defects were present but not explanatory.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The pattern is adjacent to proof-burden inversion, correction-memory-versus-infusion, process-safety barrier health, and nuclear defense-in-depth/common-mode patterns, but should not be merged until controls show whether structural load-path legibility is a distinct factor axis.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

evidence_profile.supporting_records: Five structural engineering records plus four infrastructure rails.
evidence_profile.review_depth: candidate-level synthesis only; no second-pass source edition or control set.
limitations: No positive or negative controls yet.
No recommendation-closure or code-change adoption records yet.
Champlain remains preliminary/open and must not be treated as final causal evidence.

positive_controls_needed: A structural hazard detected by peer review, load rating, inspection, confidential reporting, or records audit before failure.
A recommendation/code-change record showing that lessons from a prior structural failure measurably changed later design or inspection practice.
negative_controls_needed: A collapse where load-path/review/inspection/records rails were adequate and the dominant cause lies outside this pattern.
A structural failure caused primarily by an external extreme hazard beyond design basis rather than hidden critical-state legibility.
counterexamples_to_seek: Cases where visible cracks/corrosion or known design changes were correctly interpreted and closure/repair occurred in time.
Cases where a bridge/building collapsed despite exhaustive records, independent review, and correct inspection because of an unforeseen material or external event.
Evidence that building collapses, bridge collapses, and construction-stage failures are too heterogeneous for one shared structural legibility pattern.
rollback_triggers: If future controls show the pattern collapses into generic proof-burden or correction-infusion patterns without structural-specific content.
If Champlain final report contradicts or materially revises the preliminary use made in this candidate pattern.
If the pattern is used as a slogan against engineers, inspectors, owners, or regulators rather than as a precise factor axis.

maturity_gate.minimum_cases: 5 support records plus 2 positive controls plus 2 negative controls plus at least 2 recommendation/code-change/adoption audits
maturity_gate.required_evidence: official investigations, design/inspection/load-rating records, code/recommendation history, and explicit counterexamples

handling_notes: Do not turn structural failures into blame stories or casualty spectacle.
Do not treat Champlain preliminary findings as final cause.
Respect the difference between original design, construction change, inspection, maintenance, owner action, regulator oversight, and investigation limits.

unknowns: No positive or negative controls yet.
next_actions: Add positive control records for intercepted structural hazards.
Add negative-control records that pressure-test the pattern boundaries.
Create recommendation-closure child records for NIST/NTSB/FHWA outcomes.

revision_history.note: Created as rev0025 structural/civil failure pattern candidate.
